To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of high-resolution dynamic data on contacts is essential to model the spread and containment of epidemics and that the most appropriate representation of such data is a matrix of probability distributions of the contact duration.

The epidemic dynamics of an infectious disease model can be approximated by using a contact matrix that represents the contact durations between role-classes, but only when these are modeled as probability distributions, not as average values."

a contact matrix of average contact durations fails to reproduce the spreading properties of the epidemics obtained by using a high-resolution contact matrix, while a matrix that takes into account probability distributions of contact durations between classes of individuals can reproduce the spreading properties obtained by simulating an SEIR model directly on top of the high-resolution contact matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the definition of a new kind of contact matrices, that we refer to as "contact probability matrices", that are able to preserve some of the most important properties of the contact patterns, while providing a compact representation that allows the application of standard computational methods.

the development of mathematical representations of high-resolution contact data that can be used to inform computational models of infectious disease spread, while preserving the main epidemic properties of the data.

the development of a new framework for the integration of empirical data and computational models, with the ultimate goal to improve the understanding of epidemic spreading and design more effective containment policies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of contact matrices is a good approximation of high-resolution contact networks, provided that the matrices are constructed using a probability distribution of durations rather than a single average value, and that the role classes are chosen carefully to preserve as much information as possible about the network topology and the contact durations.
, in this case, the contact matrix representation of the contact data is not sufficient to correctly model the spread of the infection in a hospital ward.
a good representation of the data is a necessary condition to achieve a realistic simulation of the spread of a pathogen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the contact matrix is a good representation of the empirical data, but the probability distribution contact matrix is a better representation of the empirical dynamics.

, when dealing with high-resolution data, the best way to represent the contact patterns is to use a contact matrix of distributions, which is more accurate than the traditional average contact matrix.

the use of high-resolution contact data in computational models of epidemics is feasible, and the results are not only qualitatively but also quantitatively comparable to those obtained using simpler contact matrices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when dealing with high-resolution data, it is important to carefully select the representation of the contact patterns used as input to the computational models.

, in order to preserve these properties in a compact representation, the contact matrix must be able to capture not only the average duration of contacts between classes, but also the distribution of contact durations within each class and the heterogeneity of the contact durations across classes.
the choice of the contact pattern representation to be used to inform a model of disease spreading is a crucial aspect of model design that should be addressed in each specific case.
